To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of game-level parameters is essential for the design of fitness functions in the Neuroevolution approach to the imitation of human-like play.
the use of more elaborated game parameters improves the imitation of human-like play, and that the inclusion of a reward function based on the final score is the most important feature in this sense.

(1) using raw data extracted directly by a human player as input for training the artificial agent is not enough, (2) using game-level information, as the final score or the average distance to ghosts, is not enough, and (3) a combination of both approaches, raw data and game-level information, is the best option for imitating humanlike play.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a Neuroevolutionary approach for the development of virtual agents that can imitate human play.
developing an evolutionary approach to the problem of simulating human-like behaviour in computer games.

the following issues: (1) how to design a fitness function that can be used to train a Neuroevolved player; (2) how to compare different methodologies for the design of such a fitness function; and (3) how to compare the resulting players in terms of the phenomenological evaluation of their behaviour by human spectators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of game-level parameters is a good approach for the design of a fitness function that is useful to train a virtual player to imitate human behaviour.
the use of raw data from human players, as opposed to more elaborated game parameters, produces more realistic results.
the use of raw data is more effective than using elaborated game-level data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
both approaches are able to generate human-like play, but the one using the more elaborated features is able to imitate human play better.
the first methodology is more suitable to imitate human-like play, while the second one is more appropriate for learning to play the game.
the use of raw data is not necessary for imitating the behaviour of human players.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the best results are obtained when using the game-level parameters.
the use of raw data from the traces of real players is not enough to obtain good imitation results.
the use of raw data is more important than game-level features, and that it is necessary to consider a wide range of fitness function parameters to find the best one.
